note: Loeb breaks after 'the Lacedaemonians'. Jowett packs that into 'Lacedaemonian rule', and 'rule is strip or depart' is the order to go or strip.

note: Jowett puts the agreement ('a more definite understanding') before 'establish the principle', which the Loeb still has before the break.

note: The new section is the comparison with other men; Jowett's 'than the unjust' is that comparison.

start: which they will, but only what they
note: 'which they will' answers 'that they wish to do', after 'they do nothing'.

start: Do you not recollect that there was one
note: The second sentence is what he had said, the one form of holy and unholy. The first sentence is still the request for the form.

start: that the double space should have a double
note: The section opens on the claim he would have repeated: the double space needs a double side.

start: I ask no quarter at your hands. But
note: New sentence. 'I ask no quarter' is the section onset; the challenge to cheat ends the previous section.

start: the guilty are to be unpunished, but they
note: 'the guilty are to be unpunished' is the claim they do not dare, after 'argue that'.

start: in the sphere of the visible consists of
note: 'in the sphere of the visible' is 'of the visible world', and 'consists of images' follows.

start: which is not confined to the poets, but is
note: The relative clause is 'employed by both laymen and poets': prose writers as well as poets.

start: those of which I was just now speaking.
note: Jowett recasts 'not worth counting, but only what I described' as a comparison. 'those of which I was just now speaking' is what he had described.

start: Neither are the two arts of music and
note: The section is the denial of the usual purpose. 'Neither... really designed' is that denial; the subject only renames music and gymnastic.

start: matters of such importance. He or any
note: 'matters of such importance' is 'such important matters'. The 'in' before it is still the previous section.

start: that which they had never learned themselves?
note: 'that which they had never learned' is 'what they did not learn themselves'.

start: or left us behind them.
note: 'or left us behind them' is 'or whether we are left behind'. The passage ends on this phrase.

start: comes debt and the cutting down of his
note: 'Then' matches 'after this' before the break. 'comes debt and the cutting down' is 'there are borrowings and levyings'.

start: all sorts of vessels, and statues and figures
note: 'all sorts of vessels' are the implements carried past the wall. 'which appear over the wall' is the same point, placed later.

start: For this is the way of happiness.
note: This sentence is 'for this is the greatest happiness for man', after the counsel to choose the mean in this life and the next.

start: and is therefore called imera, from imeros, desire.
note: 'and is therefore called imera' is 'and so they called it himera'.

start: or of gently advising them; which varieties may
note: 'or of gently advising them' is the gentler exhortation, and the admonition clause continues the section.

start: to be called, not only poets, orators, legislators,
note: The title-clause is the new section: called not only by the writing-names but by a higher name from the serious pursuit. 'then they are' carries the pre-break 'ought'.
The window opens at 'allowing them to be drowned', later in the speech. Bringing home passenger, wife, children, and goods, and the two-drachma fee, stand before this window.

start: nay more, that to speak as we did
note: 'nay more' opens the claim that a vigorous joint act of bad men is not strictly true, after their incapacity for common action.

start: and therefore, I do not know the truth
note: 'and therefore I do not know the truth' is 'and so I do not know what the truth is', after the one-drachma course.

start: will believe that I might have saved you
note: 'will believe that I might have saved you' is what people who do not know them will think.

start: to difference and opposition, and by introducing
note: After 'puts an end', 'to difference and opposition' is 'to the differences between opposites', and number then makes the harmony.

note: The quoted 'What good? Let Gorgias answer' is the new question. 'he will go on and ask' is the lead-in.

start: you have answered a question which I have
note: 'you have answered a question' is what must come before Socrates will listen; 'not until' is before the break.

start: how you can best answer me.
note: Jowett compresses 'try to reply to my questions to the best of your belief' into 'try how you can best answer me'. 'try' is before the break.

start: or by any other sense, then, as we
note: 'or by any other sense' is 'or apprehended by some other sensation', after 'seen by itself' / 'by the sight'.

start: never get up from a sick bed? I
note: 'never get up from a sick bed' is 'never arise from their bed of sickness'. 'many a man better' is the clause before the break.

start: and a maker of rhetoricians, let me ask
note: 'and a maker of rhetoricians' is 'and to be able to make anyone else a rhetorician'.

start: and there will be less of this scandalous
note: 'less of this scandalous money-making' is the pursuit of wealth becoming less shameless, after contracts at the contractor's risk.

start: I shall have nothing to say in the
note: 'I shall have nothing to say in the justice court' opens the section, after refusing the pretty arts.

start: two out of the three lives which have
note: Jowett sets 'which have been proposed' inside the new claim. 'two out of the three... are neither sufficient' is 'of two of them neither is sufficient'.

note: The Homer line opens the section. 'when he says' is the lead-in before the break.

start: able to take every crooked turn, and wriggle
note: 'able to take every crooked turn' begins the dodges and escapes. 'master in dishonesty' is the cleverness at unjust acts, before the break.

start: and that injustice which, if it have the
note: 'injustice which, if it have the power, will murder others' is 'something that kills others when it can', after 'the contrary'.

start: and the sciences which they learned without any
note: 'the sciences which they learned without any order' brought together is the gathering of the disconnected studies, after the higher honour.

start: And now, having such an auxiliary, you must
note: 'And now, having such an auxiliary' is 'with such an aid to back you'. 'that is all' closes the offer of help.
